name: Mantle
_about: A MANTLE: a great rectangle of cloth wrapped round the body over the arms -- the Greek himation and chlamys, the Roman toga and palla -- as a cape over the shoulders and the mantle hanging from them clear of the arms down to `to`, both OPEN where the wrap is not: `centre` the middle of the cloth round the body (0 the front, 180 the back; off the back, it is wrapped from one side and pinned or tucked on the other), `span` how far round it goes. A hem band may border it (the toga's purple). `pleats`: its folds round the body (the cape over the shoulders 0.7 of them) -- a mantle is wide, and a dozen folds round it read as a board. `cascade`: the ends of the cloth down its opening hang in zigzag folds, teeth that far out every `cascadeStep` down (0: a straight edge). `cling`: how far it is DRAPED (shell.js CLING) -- over the upper arms it covers and over the legs, the share of its cone's flare it takes in (never more than what clings under it: a gown's; the cape's own, `capeCling`, whole: it lies on the shoulders), so it lies on the shoulders and falls from the elbows, a knee pushing it out, not a lampshade's cone flaring from the shoulders. OVER ONE SHOULDER (`over` "left" or "right"; true: both): the cape covers that shoulder alone (`capeCentre`, `capeSpan`; down to `capeTo`, over the shoulder's round onto the upper arm -- to the arm's top it was a flat plate out to the shoulder, shown wherever the mantle's edge falls below it), the mantle clears that arm alone -- the other free outside it -- and its top edge falls `drop` metres from that shoulder across the body to under the other arm, as the himation and the toga are worn (`edgeHigh`: the side its edge falls from, that shoulder unless it says another -- the palla, over both, wrapped from the left). Seated, its body is wrapped round the legs (`lap`: people.js, a lap over the thighs and a fall before the shins).
